title: Make metadata byte-stable
hints: Byte identity requires a serialization policy.
Sort keys and choose separators before hashing.
Reject nonfinite numbers and include the terminal newline.

title: Hash large artifacts incrementally
hints: The digest should not depend on read chunk boundaries.
Update one hash state across bounded reads.
An empty file still has a well-defined digest.

title: Bound artifact paths
hints: Check resolved containment rather than string prefixes.
Reject parent traversal before resolving symlinks.
The resolved target must be a regular file under the resolved root.

title: Describe an explicit bundle
hints: Select the bundle boundary explicitly.
Sort paths and record both size and digest.
Copy metadata so caller mutations cannot rewrite the manifest.

title: Verify integrity before use
hints: Byte size is necessary but not sufficient.
Validate every listed object’s digest as well as its path.
Equal-length corruption must fail.

title: Register immutable content
hints: A content-addressed object must match its own name.
Copy to a temporary file and verify before publication.
An already present but corrupted object is an error, not a cache hit.

title: Validate evaluation evidence
hints: Bind the report to both model and dataset.
Recompute its aggregate from unique per-case scores.
A correct digest does not excuse an inconsistent accuracy or count.

title: Encode a release policy
hints: Separate comparability checks from policy failures.
Apply evidence size, quality floor and regression limits in declared order.
An exactly satisfied threshold passes.

title: Route a stable canary cohort
hints: Assignment must survive retries and process restarts.
Convert a stable salted digest into a unit interval bucket.
The same salt makes larger fractions extend the existing cohort.

title: Summarize serving observations
hints: Keep failed requests in operational accounting.
Sort latencies before applying the stated percentile rule.
The nearest-rank index is based on all observations.

title: Decide when to roll back
hints: Decide whether there is enough evidence before applying thresholds.
Either excessive errors or excessive latency can trigger rollback.
Threshold equality is a keep decision after the minimum count.

title: Promote with compare-and-swap
hints: Atomic visibility and concurrent decision safety are different.
Lock, reread, compare the expected version, then replace.
An idempotent promotion must not erase the earlier previous pointer.

title: Restore the previous release
hints: Rollback is another version-checked promotion.
Read the prior digest but preserve the expected-current check.
A concurrent change must reject the stale rollback.

title: Release from verified evidence
hints: Bind evidence to actual model bytes before changing active state.
Run validation and the quality policy before registering artifacts.
Promotion still needs compare-and-swap even after every quality check passed.
